newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Offshore dollar sales late on Tuesday afternoon helped the rand retrace to firmer levels towards the close after importer demand initially took the unit weaker in morning trade.
Dealers said unconfirmed rumours of Reserve Bank intervention at the 4.5425 level against the dollar helped push the local unit back below 4.54.
The rand closed at 4.5365/5415 on the dollar from a 4.5300/5350 finish on Monday
"The rand was well supported at the 4.5425 level. It looked like the market had run itself long at that level and some dollars started coming in, mainly from foreigners," a dealer said.
"The Reserve Bank was certainly showing some interest there, although it did not look like direct intervention."
The Reserve Bank was unavailable for comment on Tuesday afternoon.
Dealers said there had been good two-way trade during the day with importer demand met by foreign dollar sales.
They said they expected the local unit to retrace back to around the 4.5250 level on Wednesday.
"Technically the rand is running out of steam on the overboard levels. A retracement to the 4.5250-25 level will not surprise us," a trader said.
Against the crosses the local unit edged a touch firmer to last trade at 7.0864/0987 from 7.0888/0988 against sterling late on Monday and at 0.3361/3366 from 0.3359/3364 marks previously.
On the bond market, yields climbed to near their worst levels of the day at the close in busy trade on poor sentiment about the rand and as technical factors came into play.
The key R150 bond was last at 15.305 pct from 15.12 pct at 1400 GMT on Monday.
"People are not happy about the ever-so-touchy rand, especially foreigners," a trader said.
Dealers said foreign sales of bonds had been evident during the afternoon. "We saw at least 100 million being taken out in one deal," said one.
A technical break above the 15.27 percent level spurred on further weakness, pushing the R150 to the day's weakest level of 15.31 pct in late trade.
Traders said bonds were expected to perk up on Wednesday on the back of a slightly improved rand. "We have already seen a bit of institutional nibbling," one said.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners bought a net 58.59 million rand worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying a net 120.35 million rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 4.79 billion rand from 3.42 billion rand on Friday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.70 to 15.90 percent, while 90-day BAs were unchanged at 15.15 to 15.30 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the daily shortage substantially higher at 9.28 billion rand on Monday from 7.85 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
